title: Scaling Decision Optimization to 100 Million Variables and Beyond with mPDLP in NVIDIA cuOpt | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA cuOpt's new mPDLP solver distributes huge linear programs across NVLink-connected GPUs using min-cut partitioning of the constraint matrix, with up to 11.4x speedup on PDLP steps (4.2x end-to-end) and partner results from Kinaxis (3.3x on 135M variables) and PSR (5x+ on 185M variables).

insights.claim: Today's largest planning problems in supply chain and energy can take hours to converge or exceed single-GPU memory, which bottlenecks business decision workflows even though single-GPU cuOpt already delivers over 10x speedup versus CPU solvers on large LPs.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Multi-GPU optimization extends GPU solver relevance to the largest enterprise planning workloads.

insights.claim: PDLP's hot loop is a sparse matrix-vector multiplication (SpMV) that is memory-bound, so adding GPUs multiplies available bandwidth, with NVLink, NVSwitch and NCCL making multiple GPUs act as one fast shared machine.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: NVLink-scale fabrics are the enabling hardware for distributed first-order solvers, supporting NVIDIA's interconnect moat.

insights.claim: mPDLP uses min-cut partitioning that jointly considers the two consecutive SpMVs per iteration and keeps tightly connected dependencies on the same GPU, whereas prior D-PDLP computes each SpMV independently with 2D partitioning.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Algorithmic improvement over 2D partitioning is the differentiator; performance depends on edge-cut ratios.

insights.claim: mPDLP reduces peak memory per GPU by up to 6x versus single-GPU PDLP for LPs capped at 2.1 billion nonzeros.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Allows models that do not fit on a single GPU.

insights.claim: mPDLP speedups over single-GPU cuOpt strongly correlate with problem size, becoming noticeable above 10^7 nonzeros; PDLP steps alone reach up to 11.4x on tsp-gaia-10m, versus 4.2x end-to-end once presolve, transpose, partitioning and postsolve overheads are included.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Distinguishes headline kernel speedups from end-to-end gains.

insights.claim: On most large instances (nnz above 10^7), mPDLP achieves 1.2x to 2.5x speedup over D-PDLP, but is slower than D-PDLP on the three ultra-large-scale instances, which may not represent real-world sparsity patterns.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Mixed results against the prior multi-GPU approach, limiting generality.

insights.claim: Multi-GPU PDLP helps only when problems are large enough that communication overhead is negligible versus compute, and high edge-cut ratios after partitioning can neutralize or reverse the speedup.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Rule of thumb for when multi-GPU solving pays off; small and unstructured problems will not benefit.
insights.locator: Multi-GPU PDLP delivers speedups only when problems are large enough

insights.claim: The zib03 LP benchmark with over 104 million nonzeros is now solved nearly 10x faster than a year earlier using mPDLP on multiple GPUs.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Benchmark progress shows rapid algorithm-plus-hardware improvement.

insights.claim: Kinaxis achieved a 3.3x speedup on a CPG supply chain LP with over 135M variables using mPDLP on its Maestro platform with eight NVLink-connected H100 GPUs.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Early customer validation in supply chain planning software.

insights.claim: PSR demonstrated more than 5x speedup on a stochastic energy expansion LP with 185M variables using eight NVLink-connected B200 GPUs.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Energy-system capacity-expansion modeling is a GPU-solver use case.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's planned mPDLP improvements are load-aware weight and hypergraph partitioning, overlapping communication with computation, and feasibility polishing that trades optimality for speed to solve more problems within practical limits.
insights.speaker: Bulle Mostovoi
insights.so_what: Roadmap items suggest further speedups ahead.
